forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Lambeth's £116m exceptional financial support approved in principle, with asset sales to fund it
news_drafts.lead:
Lambeth Council's application for £116m of exceptional financial support was approved in principle by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG), according to the council's second-quarter financial performance report for 2026/27. Exceptional financial support is government permission to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending. The support covers 2024/25 to 2026/27, in declining amounts.

The report says the support allowed the council to increase its reserves and provisions, to meet the 2025/26 overspend and to balance the 2026/27 budget. It also says the support lets the council treat day-to-day spending as capital spending, which is then financed by borrowing or capital receipts. If borrowing is used, interest and minimum revenue provision follow. Minimum revenue provision is the amount a council must set aside from each year's budget to pay off past borrowing.

The report states: "The Council expects to fund EFS by a planned programme of asset disposals which would reduce this figure." The quarter 2 budget monitor describes the programme as "aimed at repaying Exceptional Financial Support (EFS)" and covers the general fund and the housing revenue account, the ring-fenced account for council housing. The disposal pipeline is in Appendix C, which is exempt from publication. The report says MHCLG will scrutinise progress on asset sales and savings delivery.

news_drafts.headline: Lambeth's £116m exceptional financial support approved in principle, with asset sales planned
news_drafts.lead:
Lambeth Council's application for £116m of exceptional financial support, which is government permission to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending, has been approved in principle by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. The council's quarter 2 financial performance report for 2026/27 says so in the papers for Cabinet's meeting on 25 November. The support covers 2024/25 to 2026/27 in declining amounts, and the quarter 2 budget table shows £20m of it.

The paper says the support was used to increase reserves and provisions, meet the 2025/26 overspend and balance the 2026/27 budget. It says "the Council expects to fund EFS by a planned programme of asset disposals". Any disposal decisions will follow the council's Strategic Asset Management Framework and formal approval. A separate quarter 2 budget monitor gives an update on the disposals programme, which it describes as "aimed at repaying" the support, alongside the forecast capital spend for the year. The list of assets in the disposal pipeline is in a Part II appendix that is exempt from disclosure, and the extract gives no total.

Because Lambeth is an exceptional financial support council, the paper says "an independent third-party review is currently being undertaken by" the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy. The Ministry will scrutinise progress on asset sales and savings delivery, and the council expects regular meetings with it.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix 1 - September 26 (Q2) Financial Performance Report 2026-27 FINAL

news_drafts.headline: Lambeth's £40m exceptional support loan from 2025/26 is to be repaid from housing asset disposals
news_drafts.lead:
Lambeth received £40m of exceptional financial support in 2025/26 and must repay it, according to the Asset Management Strategy put to its Overview and Scrutiny Committee on 24 November 2026. Exceptional financial support is government permission to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending. The report names the sale of housing revenue account assets as the route to repayment. The housing revenue account is the ring-fenced account for the council's own housing stock, paid for by rents. The assets in question are those that are non-operational or beyond economic repair.

The report says the council "received £40m of Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) to address its disrepair backlog. This funding is a loan and therefore repayable." It also says no further request for exceptional financial support is currently anticipated for 2026/27.

The strategy sets out the sales so far and those planned. Residential disposals achieved £3.318m in 2025/26. Garages, land, residential properties and hostels valued at more than £13m have been identified and recommended for disposal this financial year. The report says they would come to market around the fourth quarter of 2026/27. Income from disposals is to be applied to repaying the loan.

findings.headline: Flexible use of capital receipts is set at up to £5.170m to support budget proposals
findings.detail: The report asks members to note the use of capital receipts flexibility to fund the development and implementation of budget proposals.
findings.matters: Capital receipts flexibility to fund revenue transformation is a route other councils use, and the amount is a benchmark for comparison.
findings.quote: To note the use of flexible use of capital receipts to support the development and implementation of budget proposals up to a value of £5.170m.

findings.headline: Adult Social Care forecasts a £0.974m favourable variance at Quarter 2, an improvement on Quarter 1's broadly balanced position
findings.detail: The paper attributes the position to growth funding added to the 2026/27 base budget and to savings delivered in 2025/26 and agreed for 2026/27. It also notes underlying demand and provider cost pressures.
findings.matters: A council reporting an underspend in a demand-led service, while flagging continued pressures, gives peers a benchmark for adult social care budgeting.
findings.figures: Adult Social Care favourable variance £0.974m; Integrated Health and Adult Social Care budget £142.136m
findings.quote: The Integrated Health and Adult Social Care Directorate is currently forecasting a £0.974m favourable variance at Quarter 2

findings.headline: The HRA forecasts a £2.510m surplus, which includes £18m of a £27m provision for housing disrepair claims
findings.detail: The paper says the forecast underspend reflects lower interest on borrowing and lower void loss, partly offset by repairs overspending on voids backlog clearance. It also says the council continues its financial recovery plan.
findings.matters: A disrepair provision that is only partly funded in the forecast is a liability a finance director or lender will want to track against the 30-year HRA business plan.
findings.figures: HRA surplus £2.510m; disrepair provision £27m, of which £18m included in the forecast; repairs overspend £2.216m
findings.quote: The forecast includes £18m of the £27m provision for Housing Disrepair costs

findings.headline: Total external debt stood at £1.118bn at 30 September 2026, down £9.2m in the quarter
findings.detail: The paper says £1.103bn of the debt is borrowing from the Public Works Loan Board and £15m is local authority borrowing.
findings.matters: A lender or peer council can see the size and composition of the council's borrowing at the end of Quarter 2.
findings.figures: total external debt £1.118bn; decrease £9.2m in the quarter; PWLB £1.103bn; local authority borrowing £15m
findings.quote: Total external debt outstanding at 30 September 2026 was £1.118bn, a decrease of £9.2m in the quarter.

findings.headline: An independent third-party review of Lambeth's finances is under way by CIPFA
findings.detail: The paper says the review follows from EFS status. It also says the council expects regular meetings with MHCLG on progress towards financial sustainability, with a focus on asset sales and the delivery of savings.
findings.matters: A CIPFA review of an EFS council is a governance step that other councils and lenders will want to see the outcome of.
findings.quote: an independent third-party review is currently being undertaken by CIPFA

daily_post.headline: SME invoices paid within 10 days reached 71% in Quarter 2, against an 80% target and up from 64% in Quarter 1.
daily_post.lead: Payment performance to SMEs is a supplier-market indicator that finance officers and lenders monitor alongside the council's cash management.
